items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 7.Bd2 is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Bd2.
White's king is in check from the queen on a5.
Kd1 is at least 100 centipawns below the top move at depth 16.
Nc3 is at least 60 centipawns below the top move at depth 16.

hints: You are in check. List every way to answer it: capture, block, or move the king.
A block that also brings a new piece into the game is worth comparing with moving the king.
The bishop from c1 can block on d2.
items.explain: The queen on a5 gives check along the diagonal, so White must answer it. In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine puts the block 7.Bd2 first; 7.Nc3 and 7.Kd1 are rated lower by at least 60 and 100 centipawns. That is evidence for the game move, not proof that it is the only good one.

feedback_by_move.e1d1: Moving the king is rated at least 100 centipawns below Bd2 at depth 16.
feedback_by_move.e4c3: Blocking with the knight is rated at least 60 centipawns below Bd2 at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 8.O-O-O is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is castling queenside.
Two black pieces attack the knight on e4 (the queen on e5 and the knight on f6).
One white piece defends the knight on e4 (the queen on d3).
f3 is at least 100 centipawns below the top move at depth 16.

hints: Count the attackers and defenders of the knight on e4 before you choose.
Which of your pieces is still at home without a job, and which square would it like?
One move gets the king out of the centre and puts a rook on the d-file.
items.explain: The knight on e4 is attacked twice and defended once, by the queen. In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine puts 8.O-O-O first, more than 100 centipawns above the pawn move 8.f3. The castling also puts the rook on d1, on the same file as the queen and bishop. Evidence at depth 16, not proof.

feedback_by_move.f2f3: Defending the knight with the pawn is rated at least 100 centipawns below castling at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 9.Qd8+ is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Qd8+.
Qd8+ leads to a forced mate in three (engine, depth 16).
The black knight on e4 attacks White's bishop on d2.
Rde1 is at least 500 centipawns below the top move at depth 16.

hints: Black's knight on e4 attacks your bishop on d2. Before you save it, list every check you have.
One check puts the queen on a square where only the king can take it. Ask what the king's capture does to the d-file.
The queen goes to d8 with check; after the king takes, the bishop on d2 can move with a check of its own.
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine rates 9.Qd8+ as a forced mate in three and every other move far lower. The queen is given up, and after the king takes it White has two more checks. Evidence at depth 16, not proof of the whole line.

feedback_by_move.d1e1: Rde1 is rated at least 500 centipawns below Qd8+ at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 10.Bg5+ is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Bg5+.
Bg5+ leads to a forced mate in two (engine, depth 16).
After Bg5+ two white pieces attack the king on d8: the bishop and the rook.
Bf4 is at least 500 centipawns below the top move at depth 16.

hints: The king took the queen. Which of your pieces now looks at the king along a file?
Something stands between your rook and the king. Moving it with a check of its own would make two checks at once.
Move the bishop from d2 to a square where it also gives check.
items.explain: The bishop leaves the d-file, so the rook on d1 gives check, and from g5 the bishop gives check too: two attackers on d8, so Black cannot capture or block and must move the king. The engine at depth 16 calls it mate in two; 10.Bf4 attacks the queen but is rated at least 500 centipawns lower.

feedback_by_move.d2f4: Bf4 also uncovers the rook's check and attacks the queen, but at depth 16 it is rated at least 500 centipawns below Bg5+.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 11.Bd8 is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Bd8.
Bd8 is checkmate.
A black knight stands on b8.
A black bishop stands on c8.
After Bd8 one white piece defends the bishop on d8: the rook on d1.

hints: Look at the squares next to the black king. Which are covered, and which are blocked by Black's own pieces?
The rook on d1 already controls the file. A piece that lands on the file with check only has to be defended.
Put the bishop on d8: the king cannot take it because the rook defends it.
items.explain: Bd8 attacks the king on c7 and is defended by the rook on d1, so the king cannot take it. The squares b8 and c8 hold Black's own knight and bishop, which block the king's way. It is checkmate (validated).
